timeLimit: 1:00 per heat; three heats, best two count

competition.name: Competition #1: Windy City Slam (Chicago Municipal Skate Park)
competition.rules: Three heats per skater; best two heats count; runs judged on style, difficulty and variety; points deducted for falling; bronze, silver and gold medals

goals.text: Competition #1 Windy City Slam: three heats per skater, best two count, judged on style, difficulty and variety, points off for falling; bronze, silver, gold
Competition Park: to earn a medal finish with one of the top 3 scores; the average of your top two runs is your final score
goals.evidence: LP12 level panel read on Marseille and Skatestreet (same competition-park template; inferred for this park)

goals.text: At least bronze to unlock Downtown; collectibles: 2 stat points per style, Vicarious Visions logo, alien plushie

size.evidence: VG render; scale ≈ 20 px/m taken from the other THPS1 VG renders (a parked pickup in Burnside, a helicopter in Roswell); at that scale the halfpipe is ≈ 31 m long and ≈ 15 m deck to deck, which is plausible

guidance: The spawn camera frames the two-level wall + rail ledge: the first scripted line is the first thing you see (LP1 0:10:34).
Girders and hanging lights cross the whole ceiling and stay in view from the halfpipe: the overhead goal is always visible but out of reach until you have speed.
Bright orange floors (halfpipe, rail platforms, funbox) separate skate objects from the dark concrete (VG render).
Gap names describe the target (“Over The Rafters”, “Light Grind”, “Pool 2 Walkway”), so the gap list is also a hint list.
No HUD markers in the original: the competition’s style/difficulty/variety judging is the only push to visit every element.
Remake: style-specific stat points float over the ramps near spawn; the rafter stat point sits in the path of the beam grind (LP12 0:13:40).
Hidden on purpose: the ledge and room behind spawn (remake plushie) are outside the opening view.
designLogic: One room holds the whole skill set: halfpipe with spine (vert), kidney pool with hip (bowl), wall + rail ledge, elevated rails and a funbox (street). Variety judging rewards touching all of them, so the layout spreads one example of each element type around the hall.
Spawn faces a designed line. G1 even scripts the input: hold the ollie during the countdown to reach the high rail. The first second of play is a lesson.

Height is the scoring ladder: Transfer 200 and HP Transfer 250 at the coping, Over The Pipe 700 across the halfpipe, Light Grind 500 on the lowest overhead object, Rafter Rail 1000 on the girders, Over The Rafters 2000 above them.
The hardest place is overhead and reachable from only one launcher (the large quarterpipe on the spine), and only at full speed. A single gate keeps the secret readable.
The level supplies its own speed source: a rail between two quarterpipes that you hit every pass (G1 p083). A hard-to-reach spot needs a nearby, repeatable way to build speed.
The girders run on over the pool, so the overhead layer is also a route between the vert zone and the bowl zone (G1 p084).
Two-way gap pairs (Acid Drop in, Pool 2 Walkway out) teach that a ledge next to a bowl is both a launch and a landing.
One object, three verbs: the rail platforms are ground into from the walkway (700), from the pool (1000) or cleared entirely (Whoop Gap 1000). Approach, not object count, makes variety.
The remake puts its hardest collectibles (vert stat point and VV logo) on the original’s hardest line, the rafters, and adds wallplant as a recovery for landing the beam the wrong way.
The remake hides its other collectible behind the camera (room roof behind spawn, wallride + wallie). This pairs a vert secret with a street secret, and a far one with a near one.
Failure is cheap. A fall costs judges’ points, not position, and with three 1:00 heats where the best two count, one heat can be spent on a risky overhead attempt.

TAS1 wins gold with one ≈ 3 s combo per heat and only two heats. The judged score rewards a single strong combo, not time on the clock, so a competition park needs a few dense combo spots rather than a long route.
No collectibles in the original: the competition itself is the objective, and the named gaps and the overhead layer do the job of a tape (aspiration, a visible but hard target).
remakeChanges: Collectibles added to a former contest-only park: two stat points per style (vert, street, park), a Vicarious Visions logo and an alien plushie (PS12).
Gap list: PS12 adds Across The Park (manual), Around The Bend (pool grind) and Wall Gap Jr.; Pipe 2 Box Grind is not in PS12’s list. Wall Gap is on the PS1 VG map but not in G1.
The ceiling girders are lattice trusses in the remake and are skated with wallplant reversals (LP12 0:13:44–0:13:56).
Competition rules restated: a medal for a top-3 finish, the final score is the average of the top two runs; LP12 shows the remake’s “Overtime!” finish on THPS1 parks.

LP1 vs LP12: the PS1 run opens on the double rail; the LP12 heat includes a long halfpipe → spine transfer → rafter sequence (0:13:36–0:14:00), which is where the remake put its vert pickups. The remake loading card reads “That there bowl’s deeper than a couple …” (LP12 0:13:05; text partly cut off).
transfer: Rafter crystal: put the crystal at the far end of a ceiling beam above a halfpipe. The only way up is a spine transfer from a quarterpipe backed onto the halfpipe, at pumped maximum speed. A miss lands in the halfpipe and costs seconds. Tune the beam height in-engine so that cruise speed reaches only the lower rung (below).

Ladder of rungs: hang a light or a short bar under the beam about 2.4 m below it, so a grind-ollie from the rung (≈ 2.4 m pop) reaches the beam. This gives an intermediate step that teaches the vertical line before the full transfer.

Speed loop beside the goal: place a rail between two quarterpipes on the approach (as G1’s Over The Rafters setup does) or a speed pad, so the player can repeat the build-up without crossing the level.

Behind-spawn roof: a small quarterpipe up to a ledge behind the spawn camera, then wallride + wallie onto a room roof. Use it as the crystal for an easier level, or as the tease that shows the crystal’s glint from the roof.

Two-way bowl edge: a walkway beside a bowl with gaps in both directions. A crystal floating just past the walkway edge can only be taken by the vert air out of the bowl (Pool 2 Walkway), not by walking along the walkway.
openQuestions: PS1 girder height is not measurable from VG’s isometric render; LP12 suggests ≈ 7–9 m in the remake.
Is the “room with a door” behind spawn (remake plushie) present in the PS1 geometry? VG shows dark box structures on the NE walkway but no clear room.
Wall Gap is labelled on VG but missing from G1; PS12 lists it at 100. Was it added in a later PS1 build than the guide used?
Pipe 2 Box Grind is absent from PS12’s list: removed, renamed, or an omission in the guide?
G1 places the Over The Box box “in the left corner of the room”; VG shows it in the SE corner. The wording depends on viewpoint.
